Fall Off The Bone BBQ Beef Ribs - Grilled Ribs Recipe

BBQ Beef Ribs - These ribs are moist, juicy, tender, and easily slide off the bone. They are slow-cooked at a low temperature for a perfect result. They are smoky, sweet, savory, and full of flavor.

Easy Grilled Beef Back Ribs Recipe

Summer is never complete without seasoned BBQ beef ribs coated with juicy BBQ sauce. These ribs show up at every cookout, every family gathering, every celebration, and they disappear faster than anything else on the table.

I use a charcoal grill for that deep, authentic smoky flavor, but I have also included a full oven method below, because good ribs should not be limited to people who own a grill.

They can be tough to make, but here's a simple recipe for grilled beef ribs that you can try out at home. And because we make both the rub and sauce from scratch, you are in complete control of every flavor in the dish!

Why You Will Love This Recipe

  • Deep Flavor Crust: The dry rub builds a deep, caramelized crust on the outside while the slow cooking keeps the inside moist and tender.
  • Sticky Homemade Sauce: The homemade BBQ sauce is sticky, tangy, and slightly sweet, coating every inch of the meat.
  • Two Cooking Methods: Choose grilling for authentic smoky flavor, or oven baking when the weather does not cooperate. Both give fall-off-the-bone results.
  • Complete Control: Making both the rub and sauce from scratch means you control every flavor element.

Slow-cooked beef ribs

Beef ribs need to be cooked slowly at a low temperature so they have time to develop flavor and become tender and juicy. Slow cooking lets the ribs fall off the bone easily.

The grill does a great job of accomplishing all this for you. You get the nice texture and flavor of ribs, plus the mouth-watering smell. It's barbecuing at its finest

Beef ribs are done by temperature, not by clock. The target is an internal temperature of 200°F; that's when the connective tissue has fully broken down.

If your ribs come out tough, they aren't overdone; instead, they are underdone. Put them back at the same low temperature and check again in 30 minutes.

Beef ribs cannot be rushed over high heat; that tightens the muscle fibers and makes the meat chewy.

Slow grilling helps:

  1. Concentrate the flavors of the meat so much more than anything else
  2. Maintain that yummy pink color on the meat.
  3. Give that perfect caramelized char.

What Kind of Beef Ribs Should You Buy?

  • Full Slab Back Ribs: Come from the back of the cow, near the spine. Leaner and slightly less meaty than short ribs. This is what I use.
  • Short Beef Ribs: Meatier, thicker, and have more fat running through them. They are wonderful for braising, but they work here too if back ribs aren't available.

Barbeque Beef Ribs Dry Rub

For making this recipe, you can make your own rub or use the store-bought ones. I like making mine because I can control the amount of each ingredient, especially the salt.

The rub is a mixture of brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin powder, dry mustard powder, salt, and black pepper.

You can make extra and store the remainder in an airtight jar. It keeps for months and works beautifully on chicken recipes too!

Be sure to press the rub firmly into every surface of the meat. Don't just dust it on; really press it in with your hands so it adheres and forms a proper crust during cooking.

Homemade BBQ sauce

The homemade BBQ sauce is a mixture of garlic powder, apple cider vinegar, ketchup, brown sugar, black pepper, onion powder, yellow mustard powder, cayenne pepper, and apple juice.

Combine everything in a saucepan and simmer for about 8 minutes, until it thickens into a glossy syrup. Stir occasionally with a wooden spoon so it doesn't catch on the bottom.

Brush it on generously, front and back, and don't hold back. Add more during the last few minutes of cooking for an extra sticky, caramelized finish.

Ingredients for making BBQ Beef Ribs

  • Beef ribs: You can get your beef ribs at a local grocery or meat store. For this recipe, I use full slab back ribs. Two slabs feed about 4 to 6 people comfortably.
  • Olive oil: Rubbed all over before the rub goes on. Helps the rub adhere and promotes even browning.
  • Brown sugar: Adds sweetness and helps caramelize into that crust.
  • Paprika: For color and for subtle smoky warmth.
  • Garlic, Onion, and Cumin powder: Adds savory depth to the rub
  • Salt and Black pepper: Add to taste
  • Apple cider vinegar acts as an acid to help tenderize the meat. If you don't have apple cider vinegar, lemon juice works as a substitute.
  • Liquid smoke - If you're not using a charcoal grill, a small amount of liquid smoke in the sauce gives you the smoky depth you'd otherwise get from the charcoal.
  • Ketchup: The tomato base for sweetness, acidity, and body.
  • Yellow mustard powder: Tangy sharpness so the sauce isn't one-note.
  • Cayenne pepper: Add a little for a gentle heat that isn't overpowering.
  • Apple juice or water: Thins the sauce for brushing; apple juice adds fruity sweetness.

How to make Grilled Ribs Recipe

How to Make BBQ Beef Ribs

  • Step 1: Remove the membrane and trim the fat: Place the ribs bone side up. Use a butter knife or your fingers to lift the thin papery membrane from one end, grab it with a paper towel for grip if you wish, and pull it off in one piece. Pulling off the membrane will help the meat fall apart easily. Trim any large pieces of excess fat.
  • Step 2: Apply the dry rub: Drizzle olive oil over both sides and rub it in. Mix the dry rub ingredients, then apply generously to every surface, pressing firmly. Beyond flavor, the generous dry rub coating also helps protect the meat from moisture loss while grilling. Be generous! Cover with foil and set aside while making the sauce.
  • Step 3: Make the BBQ sauce: Add all sauce ingredients to a saucepan over medium heat. Stir, bring to a gentle simmer, and cook about 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until glossy and syrupy.
  • Step 4: Marinate. Brush sauce generously over the front and back of the ribs. Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours (overnight is better). If short on time, cook immediately.
  • Step 5: Grill or bake

Grill Method

  • Preheat to 275°F.
  • Place ribs meatier side down over indirect heat.
  • Cook at least 2- 3 hours, depending on the thickness of the ribs, turning every 20 minutes. You can go longer for really chunky meaty ribs!
  • Baste generously in the last 10–20 minutes.
  • Don't let the temperature fall below 250F at any point during the cooking process.

Oven-Baked Beef Ribs

If baking is convenient:

  • Preheat your oven to 325°F (163°C).
  • Place ribs on a tray, cover tightly with foil
  • Bake for 2 hours.
  • Remove the foil and bake another hour, until the internal temperature reaches 200°F.
  • For fall-off-the-bone ribs, add another 30 minutes uncovered, brushing on extra sauce during this final period.
  • Serve and enjoy.

How to Tell When the Ribs Are Done

  • Meat Thermometer: This is the most reliable way to check if the meat is done. When the internal temperature reaches 200°F, it is ready. Insert the thermometer into the thickest part of the meat, between two bones in the middle of the rack. Be careful not to let the thermometer touch the bone, as this can give you a false reading.
  • Lift the rib bone: If you don't have a thermometer to measure the internal temperature, you can gently lift the rib bone. When the rib falls off, the beef is done. If you want to try this, use a kitchen towel to prevent burns.
  • Bone Twist: Another option is to use your tongs to twist the center rib; the ribs are ready if they fall out easily.
  • Cut the meat: You can also cut into the meat to see if it is done. If there is no pink and the meat is soft, it is done.

Equipment for making BBQ Ribs

  • Gas grill with two or more burners / Oven – You need this for cooking the ribs
  • Tongs – this is for turning the ribs sideways from time to time
  • Oven thermometer – use this to check the doneness of the ribs
  • Metal drip pan – You need this to collect the liquid from the meat while baking or grilling.
  • Aluminum foil – This keeps the beef moist and prevents it from drying out. It also helps the seasoning to circulate deep into the ribs.
  • Basting brush or mopping tool – You need the brush to apply the BBQ sauce.

What to Serve with BBQ Beef Ribs

These ribs are bold and rich, so they pair best with contrast like something creamy, something fresh, or something starchy to soak up the sauce.

  • Garlic Butter Sautéed Broccoli: the bright garlicky butter cuts right through the richness of the meat
  • Baked Potato Wedges: crispy and made for dipping in leftover sauce
  • Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes: creamy, buttery, perfect for scooping up extra BBQ sauce
  • Creamy coleslaw: cool, crunchy, and the most classic BBQ pairing of all
  • Sautéed Green Beans and Bacon: smoky and savory alongside smoky and sweet
  • Sukuma Wiki: braised collard greens alongside smoky ribs is deeply satisfying
  • Creamy Parmesan Risotto: rich and velvety, and a wonderful base for the sauce to drip into
  • Breakfast Potatoes: crispy, smoky, a natural partner for anything off the grill
  • Fresh French Bread: for mopping the plate
  • Tomato Mozzarella Salad: fresh and acidic against all that richness

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I grill the ribs wrapped in foil, or uncovered?

On the grill, cook them uncovered over indirect heat so the smoke reaches the meat and the sauce caramelizes. The foil in Step 2 is only to cover the seasoned ribs while you make the sauce, not for cooking. Foil-wrapping is part of the oven method, where it stops the meat from drying out.

Can I make these ribs without a grill?

Yes. The oven method gives you the same fall-off-the-bone result. The only thing you miss is charcoal smokiness, which you can replicate with a little liquid smoke in the sauce.

How long should I marinate the ribs?

At least 2 hours gives great flavor. Overnight is better. Even 30 minutes makes a difference if that's all you have.

Why are my ribs tough?

Cooking too fast at too high a temperature, or simply not long enough, will make the ribs tough. Beef ribs need time at low heat for the connective tissue to break down. Put them back at the same temperature and check again in 30 minutes.

Do I have to remove the membrane?

Yes. It's tough, chewy, and blocks the rub from reaching the meat underneath. It takes about 30 seconds and makes a real difference.

Can I use pork ribs instead of beef?

Yes. The rub and sauce work beautifully on pork. Cooking time is slightly shorter; pork ribs are done at 190–203°F depending on how tender you want them.

Can I use store-bought sauce?

Yes, and readers have. It works. The homemade sauce gives you control over the sweetness and salt, but a very good bottled sauce will still produce good ribs.

How do I store and reheat leftovers?

Store in an airtight container or tightly wrapped in foil, and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat at 300°F covered with foil for 20–25 minutes. Brush with extra sauce first to keep them moist.

Can I freeze cooked ribs?

Yes. Wrap cooled ribs tightly in plastic, then foil, and freeze up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat as above.

Notes

  • Removing the membrane is not optional if you want truly tender ribs.
  • Press the rub firmly into the meat; real pressure means real adhesion and a proper crust.
  • Low and slow is the only way. Higher heat tightens the muscle fibers and gives you tough, chewy ribs.
  • Make extra dry rub and jar it. It keeps for months and is wonderful on chicken, pork chops, and roasted vegetables.

Fall Off the Bone BBQ Beef Ribs

Summer is never complete without seasoned BBQ beef ribs coated with juicy BBQ sauce. The ribs are slowly cooked at a low temperature to make a perfect hit. It is moist, juicy, and tender. You mustn’t miss this during your next game day, casual dinner, or family party.

Keyword: Barbecue, bbq beef ribs, Beef
Prep Time: 10 minutes minutes
Cook Time: 2 hours hours
Total Time: 2 hours hours 10 minutes minutes
Servings: 4 people
Calories: 276.8kcal

Equipment

  • Charcoal or gas grill.
  • Oven
  • Tong – this is for turning the ribs sideways from time to time
  • Oven thermometer – use this to check the doneness of the rib
  • Metal drip pan – You need this to collect the liquid from the meat while baking or grilling.
  • Aluminum foil – keeps the beef moist and prevents it from drying out. It also helps the seasoning to circulate deep into the ribs.
  • Basting brush or mopping tool – You need the brush to apply the BBQ sauce.

Ingredients

  • 2 slabs beef ribs
  • 2-4 tablespoons olive oil

Rub:

  • 2 tablespoon dark brown sugar
  • 2 teaspoon paprika
  • 1 teaspoon dry mustard
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 teaspoon onion powder
  • ½ teaspoon cumin powder
  • 1½ teaspoon salt or add to taste
  • 1 teaspoon black pepper

Barbeque sauce:

  • 1 cup ketchup
  • 5 tablespoon brown sugar
  • ¼ cup apple cider vinegar
  • 2 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 2 teaspoon onion powder
  • 2 tablespoon yellow mustard powder
  • 2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 teaspoon cayenne pepper
  • 1 cup apple juice orange juice, or water
US Customary - Metric

Instructions

Instructions:

  • Place the ribs on a wide tray or a wooden slab, pull off the membrane, and trim any excess fat.
  • Rub the oil all over the ribs. Then mix the rub ingredients in a small bowl and season the ribs generously by pressing the rub firmly onto every surface. Cover with foil while you prepare the barbecue sauce.
  • Add all the barbecue sauce ingredients to a saucepan over medium heat. Stir and simmer for about 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened and glossy. Leave to cool.
  • Brush the sauce generously over the front and back of the ribs. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours; overnight is better. If you are really short of time, you can cook immediately.

Grill method:

  • Prepare the grill and heat to 275℉.
  • Place the meatier side of the ribs down on the grill over indirect heat. Cook for at least 2 to 3 hours, depending on the thickness, turning every 20 minutes. Baste with barbecue sauce in the last 10-20 minutes of cooking.
  • Cook for an additional 30 minutes uncovered for 'really' fall-off-the-bone ribs, brushing on extra sauce during the final period.

Oven method:

  • Preheat the oven to 325°F (163°C).
  • Place the ribs on a tray, cover tightly with foil, then bake in the oven for 2 hours.
  • Uncover the foil and bake for another hour or until the ribs reach an internal temperature of 200°F. Cook for an additional 30 minutes for really ''fall-off-the-bone'' ribs.

Notes

  • Removing the membrane is not optional if you want truly tender ribs.
  • Press the rub firmly into the meat; real pressure means real adhesion and a proper crust.
  • Low and slow is the only way. Higher heat tightens the muscle fibers and gives you tough, chewy ribs.
  • Make extra dry rub and jar it. It keeps for months and is wonderful on chicken, pork chops, and roasted vegetables.
